finding.summary: `Doc.findBlockInCells` still walks the parent chain by unguarded recursion — the one parent-map walk this PR's cycle-guard sweep missed, and it is reachable from the very copy/cut path the delta fixes
finding.evidence: The delta's premise (repeated verbatim in the new comments in `peer-cursor.ts:122-128` and `selection.ts:120-125`) is that `blockParentMap` chains come from peer-written CRDT ids and can loop. Three view-side walks now carry a `seen` set (`table-layout.ts:488`, `peer-cursor.ts:128`, `selection.ts:132`, plus `text-editor.ts:3894/3919`, `range-slices.ts:81`). `document.ts:261-290` does the same walk by recursion with no visited set: `findBlockInCells(id)` looks up `cellInfo = _blockParentMap.get(id)`, fails to find `cellInfo.tableBlockId` among the top-level/header/footer arrays, and calls `this.findBlockInCells(cellInfo.tableBlockId)` at line 276. On a chain a→b→a this recurses forever and throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` out of `Doc.getBlock`/`findBlock` rather than returning undefined. It is on the same nested-table cell-range flow the delta touches: `text-editor.ts:2861` (`this.doc.getBlock(cr.blockId)` inside `forEachBlockInSelection`), `text-editor.ts:508` (`this.doc.findBlock(rect.blockId)`) and `text-editor.ts:3330` (`this.doc.getBlock(anchorCI.tableBlockId).tableData!`) all hand it an id taken straight from the same map the new guards distrust. verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: Doc.findBlockInCells (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:261-290) walks the blockParentMap parent chain by self-recursion at line 276 with no visited set and no depth bound, so a looping chain whose ids are not top-level in body/header/footer recurses until the stack overflows, throwing RangeError out of getBlock (line 236) and findBlock (line 254) instead of returning undefined. The premise that such loops are representable is the repository's own, stated in the guards on every other walk of the same map: table-layout.ts:480-495 (seen set, "a parent chain that loops back on itself ... is representable"), peer-cursor.ts:122-136 (seenTableIds), range-slices.ts:77-91 (seen in topLevelBlockId), selection.ts:116-136. No caller-side guard exists: setBlockParentMap (document.ts:136) accepts any map and is fed from editor.ts:1703 (merged body+header+footer map), text-box-editor.ts:479, and tests, none validating acyclicity. I could not prove layout-time construction is cycle-free (duplicate ids plus the last-writer-wins merges across regions/top-level tables leave it open), and per instructions that uncertainty keeps the finding. Unbounded recursion causing an uncaught exception on getBlock/findBlock paths is squarely in the correctness lane, so no refutation ground (not-present, already-guarded, out-of-scope) applies.

finding.summary: Nested-table cell rectangle still copies an empty `text/plain` flavour — `getSelectedText` keeps the flat `layout.blocks.find` lookup the diff fixed everywhere else
finding.evidence: The change patched the two flat lookups it found (`normalizeRange` at selection.ts:128-130 and `getSelectedTableCells` at text-editor.ts:4331-4333) but `Selection.getSelectedText` still does `const lb = layout.blocks.find((b) => b.block.id === cr.blockId); if (!lb?.block.tableData) return '';` (selection.ts:761-762). A nested table is not in `layout.blocks`, so this returns `''`. Both `handleCopy` (text-editor.ts:1439) and `handleCut` (text-editor.ts:1482) write that as `text/plain` right next to the WAFFLEDOCS payload — so a cell rectangle inside a nested table copies nothing to any external application, and the cut path then calls `deleteSelection()` (text-editor.ts:1484), destroying the cells with only the internal flavour holding them. The new test only asserts the WAFFLEDOCS flavour (`nested-table-cell-range.test.ts`, 'copying a nested cell rectangle writes the cells'), so this half stays uncovered.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts that `Selection.getSelectedText` still performs a flat `layout.blocks.find((b) => b.block.id === cr.blockId)` lookup with `if (!lb?.block.tableData) return '';`, causing nested-table cell rectangles to copy an empty `text/plain`. That code is not present. In the working tree, selection.ts:788-791 reads `const td = layout.blocks.find(...)?.block.tableData ?? resolveNestedTableLayout(cr.blockId, layout)?.dataBlock.tableData; if (!td) return '';` — i.e. the same nested-aware fallback used by `normalizeRange` (selection.ts:155-157), with a comment at selection.ts:784-787 explicitly citing the same issue. The cell-internal branch at selection.ts:816-821 has the identical fallback. `resolveNestedTableLayout` is imported at selection.ts:9 and defined at table-layout.ts:474-526, where it walks `blockParentMap` to the top-level table and returns the nested `dataBlock`, so `dataBlock.tableData` is populated for nested tables. The cited line numbers (selection.ts:761-762) are the signature lines of `getNormalizedRange`, not the alleged lookup. Therefore the downstream consequence (empty text/plain at text-editor.ts:1439/1482 followed by deleteSelection at 1484) does not occur. The remaining observation about test coverage is a test-quality point, outside the correctness lens.

finding.summary: The new cycle guards are bypassed: `normalizeRange`'s own parent-chain walks (and `peer-cursor.ts`) still spin forever on the same cyclic `blockParentMap` the diff says would hang the tab
finding.evidence: The diff adds `seen` sets to `resolveNestedTableLayout` (table-layout.ts:488-494), `findOuterCellAddress` (text-editor.ts:3894-3906) and `findOutermostTableId` (text-editor.ts:3919-3925) on the stated ground that a looping parent chain is representable and would hang a render. But the very function the diff edits keeps two unguarded walks: `while (anchorTopId && layout.blocks.findIndex(...) === -1) { ... anchorTopId = parentInfo.tableBlockId; }` (selection.ts:147-151) and the identical focus walk (selection.ts:153-157). With `a -> b -> a` neither id is ever in `layout.blocks`, so the loop never terminates — and this runs on every non-cell-range `normalizeRange`, i.e. every paint of an ordinary selection. `peer-cursor.ts:122-127` has the same unguarded `while (true)` walk on the render path. A tab hang is exactly the outcome the guard was added to prevent, so the protection is incomplete at the sites that need it most.

verdict.reason: The finding claims two unguarded parent-chain walks remain in selection.ts (147-157) and one in peer-cursor.ts (122-127). Neither is present in this working tree. In selection.ts the anchor/focus walks are both factored into a single helper `walkToTopLevelBlockId` (selection.ts:127-140) that maintains a `seen` set and breaks when `parentInfo.tableBlockId` repeats, so an a->b->a chain terminates and the callers (selection.ts:173-183) then fail the `findIndex` check and return null. In peer-cursor.ts the `while (true)` walk at 129-136 initializes `seenTableIds` with the starting table id and `return undefined` on a repeat before the `unshift`, so it neither spins nor grows `nestingPath`. Lines 122-127 the reviewer cites as the unguarded loop are in fact the comment documenting the guard. The other `blockParentMap` uses in selection.ts (295-296, 811-812) are single map lookups, not walks.
